And we understand that data only gains true value when it solves a real problem.
summary:
Agrohelper — Your Pocket Farming Assistant

​For generations, farmers have relied on the rhythm of the seasons to decide when to plant and harvest. Today, unpredictable droughts, sudden heatwaves, and shifting rainfall have turned every planting season into a high-stakes gamble, often without access to local agronomic advice.

​Agrohelper puts a smart, reliable advisor right in a farmer’s pocket. By simply tapping their plot on a map and sharing what they want to grow the farmer will receive step-by-step guidance tailored to their exact field. Powered by Earth observations and local weather insights, Agrohelper suggest them what to cultivate before extreme weather strikes.
​This matters because protecting a harvest shouldn’t require a science degree just the right advice at the right time to keep farms thriving.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

AgroHelper is an interactive web and mobile app built to help farmers adapt their crops to changing climate conditions using open NASA satellite data. Instead of relying solely on memory or guesswork, users can select any location on Earth and immediately receive crop compatibility scores, a 3-cycle crop rotation plan, and practical guidance from an agronomic AI assistant.

The experience follows four simple steps:

  • Select a farm on the interactive map by searching a city or region, using GPS, or clicking directly on regional or satellite imagery.
  • Analyze live climate data from NASA POWER over the past year alongside a 16-day weather forecast and water balance from Open-Meteo.
  • Explore 1,287 crops from the FAO EcoCrop database, automatically scored against local temperature, rainfall, frost risk, and elevation.
  • Review a 3-cycle rotation plan designed to alternate plant families and replenish soil nitrogen, or chat with the built-in agronomic assistant, including uploading photos of leaves, pests, or soil for preliminary visual observations.

What benefits does it have?

  • Turns complex satellite measurements into clear planting decisions for a specific parcel.
  • Helps manage water by comparing historical rainfall with short-term evapotranspiration and net water balance.
  • Protects long-term soil health by discouraging continuous monoculture and prioritizing nitrogen-fixing legumes in rotation cycles.
  • Translates scientific crop data and Latin names into plain-language guidance accessible from both desktop and mobile devices.

What is the intended impact of the project? AgroHelper aims to put space-derived agricultural intelligence directly into the hands of small and medium-scale farmers, agronomists, and rural communities—especially in areas vulnerable to droughts and heatwaves. By making climate adaptation tools accessible without specialized GIS software or paid subscriptions, the project seeks to stabilize yields, protect soil fertility, and reduce overreliance on synthetic inputs. In future phases, the platform is structured to integrate automated global soil telemetry, long-term climate projections, and NASA satellite map layers.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Languages: TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
  • Frontend and Mapping: Angular 20, RxJS, Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, Nominatim, and Esri World Imagery.
  • Backend and Hosting: Angular SSR with Express 5, Node.js 22, and Vercel Serverless Functions.
  • Data Sources: NASA POWER Daily API, Open-Meteo Forecast API, and the FAO EcoCrop dataset.
  • AI and Vision: Google Gemini API via the official GenAI SDK, paired with client-side HTML5 Canvas image compression.
  • Development and Testing: Jasmine, Karma, Git, GitHub, Visual Studio Code, and standard laptops and smartphones for responsive testing.

How is your project creative?

Rather than acting as a disconnected chatbot, AgroHelper's assistant is directly linked to the live dashboard. When a user writes a natural-language question mentioning a location and a crop, the system automatically geocodes the place, pulls live NASA climate and forecast data, evaluates the crop, and updates the map and rotation timeline in real time. The assistant is also strictly anchored to the parcel's real metrics and combines satellite data with local field observations reported by the farmer.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Satellite data reliability: Recent NASA POWER records can contain -999 fill values while awaiting processing, so we applied a 7-day lag window, filtered invalid entries, and annualized precipitation for accurate crop comparisons.
  • Local field context: Satellites alone cannot capture every soil condition or grower goal, so we added selectable soil observations, farmer priorities, and custom field notes.
  • Field accessibility and cost: Everything runs on open public APIs, a pre-compiled local crop catalog for fast loading, on-device image compression before upload, and automatic AI model fallback to handle free-tier rate limits smoothly.
  • Clarity and honesty: Where automated global soil databases are planned for a future phase, the platform clearly relies on baseline defaults and farmer-reported observations rather than inventing soil metrics.
